products.name: React Flow
products.description: React-first node-based UI framework for building interactive workflow diagrams and node-based editors. Designed for authoring workflows, dashboards, and graph-based interfaces with seamless React integration.
products.positioning: Easiest authoring experience for React developers building node-based UIs. Purpose-built for workflow/diagram workflows, not dense graph analysis.

products.name: D3.js
products.description: Low-level, modular JavaScript visualization library for data-driven document manipulation. Provides granular control over DOM/SVG/Canvas for unlimited customization of visualizations.
products.positioning: Maximum customization and flexibility at the cost of steep learning curve and effort. Foundation for many higher-level tools. SVG-based, best for medium-sized graphs.

products.name: Cytoscape.js
products.description: JavaScript library for graph analysis and visualization with comprehensive layout algorithms, styling, and network analysis capabilities. Designed for network/biology research and data analysis.
products.positioning: Best-in-class for graph analysis with 67+ layout extensions and algorithms. Academic backing, top 0.01% of software packages by adoption.

products.name: Sigma.js
products.description: WebGL-based graph visualization library designed for large-scale network visualization with thousands of nodes and edges. Integrates with Graphology data structure library.
products.positioning: GPU-accelerated rendering for large graphs (thousands of nodes). Renderer + data layer; not batteries-included on algorithms.

products.name: vis.js
products.description: Dynamic browser-based visualization library with Network, Timeline, Graph2d, and Graph3d components. Includes physics simulation and clustering for interactive network exploration.
products.positioning: Ease-of-use sweet spot for quick interactive network visualizations. Physics simulation and clustering help with large graphs but Canvas limits at ~1k nodes with full interactivity.

products.name: react-force-graph
products.description: React bindings for force-graph suite with 2D, 3D, VR, and AR variants. Canvas/WebGL rendering of force-directed graphs with extensive customization.
products.positioning: Specialized for force-directed layouts in multiple dimensions (2D/3D/VR/AR). Limited to force-directed algorithm.

products.name: Cosmograph
products.description: Commercial GPU-accelerated graph visualization platform with DuckDB integration, linked brushing, timeline features, and cross-filtering for interactive network exploration.
products.positioning: Performance-first commercial platform bridging DB query and visualization. DuckDB-native. Free for non-commercial use.

products.name: Ogma
products.description: Commercial enterprise JavaScript graph visualization SDK with GPU acceleration, 8+ layout algorithms, built-in graph algorithms, and professional support. Designed for production-scale deployments.
products.positioning: Enterprise-grade scalability (100k+ edges), support, and advanced layouts. Competes on production-readiness vs open source.

competitors.wedge_vs_them: React Flow is purpose-built for workflow authoring. MetroGraph targets DB visualization + graph-based query interfaces (RAG/agent builders) where dense relational networks matter more than workflow linearity. MetroGraph's strength is surface-area reduction (integrated search, filter, drill-down) vs React Flow's strength (smooth authoring DX for users designing workflows/diagrams).
competitors.moat: Strong React ecosystem position. 36k+ GitHub stars. xyflow company backing and open source community.

competitors.wedge_vs_them: D3 is low-level primitive for custom visualization. MetroGraph is a graph-centric UI platform with integrated search/query/filter. D3 requires significant engineering to build graph authoring/analysis UX; MetroGraph provides that out-of-box.
competitors.moat: Unparalleled customization. 113k+ GitHub stars. Observable platform + community.

competitors.wedge_vs_them: Cytoscape is graph analysis library for biology/network science. MetroGraph targets data engineers + RAG/agent builders where graph-as-query-interface matters. Cytoscape assumes you want to analyze the graph; MetroGraph assumes you want to query a DB via graph metaphor. Cytoscape's 67+ layouts are academic; MetroGraph's layout is data-driven (results of query).
competitors.moat: Academic research backing. University of Toronto. Peer-reviewed updates. 67+ layout extensions.

competitors.wedge_vs_them: Sigma is WebGL renderer for large graphs. MetroGraph is a graph DB visualization + query interface. Sigma is rendering layer + Graphology data model; MetroGraph integrates query execution (SQL/Cypher), authoring, filtering. Sigma excels at rendering millions of nodes; MetroGraph excels at making those nodes mean something (search, filter, drill-down on relationships).
competitors.moat: WebGL performance. Graphology integration. Active open source development.

competitors.wedge_vs_them: vis.js is easy-to-use interactive diagram library with physics. MetroGraph is query-driven DB visualization. vis.js is good for static network exploration; MetroGraph is designed for dynamic query results + authoring workflows. vis.js hits performance ceiling at 1k nodes; MetroGraph scales to tens of thousands.
competitors.moat: Low friction for quick prototypes. Physics simulation. Interactive defaults.

competitors.wedge_vs_them: react-force-graph specializes in force-directed 2D/3D/VR/AR visualization. MetroGraph is graph query + authoring platform. Neither competes head-to-head: react-force-graph is for specialized spatial/3D use cases; MetroGraph is for graph-as-query-interface.
competitors.moat: Unique 2D/3D/VR/AR positioning. ThreeJS backend. Canvas + WebGL variants.

competitors.wedge_vs_them: Cosmograph is GPU-accelerated graph visualization platform with DuckDB integration. Both target DB-centric visualization. Cosmograph's wedge: performance + native DuckDB bridge. MetroGraph's wedge: integrated graph authoring + AI-powered exploration (agents, RAG, prompt-to-visualization). Cosmograph excels at rendering; MetroGraph excels at interaction + orchestration.
competitors.moat: GPU performance. DuckDB native integration. Commercial support. Timeline linked-brushing.

competitors.wedge_vs_them: Ogma is commercial enterprise graph visualization SDK. Both scale to 100k+ edges. Ogma's wedge: production-grade layouts + algorithms + support. MetroGraph's wedge: AI-powered workflows + surface-area reduction (integrated search/filter/explore). Ogma is a better visualization library for static/pre-computed graphs; MetroGraph is better for dynamic DB-driven exploration + authoring.
competitors.moat: Enterprise sales + support. Established vendor. Professional SDKs. Comprehensive layout + analysis suite. Linkurious ecosystem.

notes: Competitive Leaf: Graph/Node Rendering Libraries. Scope: 7 primary open-source libraries (React Flow, D3.js, Cytoscape.js, Sigma.js, vis.js, react-force-graph, Cosmograph) vs MetroGraph. Key HCI insight from Cambridge Intelligence + Memgraph research: hairball/visual-clutter problem is universal across rendering libraries. Sigma/Cosmograph solve via GPU scaling; D3/Cytoscape solve via layout algorithms; React Flow sidesteps via workflow-linear design. MetroGraph's differentiation: AI-powered node suggestion + surface-area reduction (search/filter before visualization) addresses the root HCI pain point that no library alone solves. Threat assessment: React Flow (authoring UX parity needed), Cytoscape (layout algorithm integration), Sigma/Cosmograph (performance at scale + DuckDB native), Ogma (enterprise FUD). Product-feature scoring reflects: (1) relevance to MetroGraph's ICP (data engineers + startup builders), (2) maturity/production-readiness, (3) HCI friction for each capability. Open-source libraries show strong rendering but weaker at integrated workflows; commercial (Ogma/Cosmograph) show strong production posture but weaker at authoring/AI-assist.
